text: THE National University of Singapore and Sunway University have been named Aseans No. 1 public and private universities, respectively, in the AppliedEdu University Rankings 2027 for Asean. NUS leads the public university rankings for the third consecutive year, while Sunway University retains the private university top spot for the fourth consecutive year. Malaysia claims seven of the top ten private university positions and five of the top ten public university positions. It also has more institutions in the top 50 of each category than any other country, with 21 private and 16 public universities. The 2027 edition is AppliedEdus most comprehensive South-East Asian higher education assessment yet, ranking 316 universities across nine Asean countries, up 33% from last year. It draws on over 100,000 validated student responses, academic peer nominations and verified institutional data. The results were announced in conjunction with AppliedEduXChange 2026, which brought together more than 150 university leaders under the theme Beyond Skills: Building Employable, Industry-Ready Graduates. Being named Aseans No. 1 private university for the fourth consecutive year is a proud moment for Sunway University and for Malaysia. Our ambition is for every graduate to leave with the knowledge, confidence and experience to build a meaningful career and contribute positively to society. That is what being a mission-driven Fifth Generation University means to us. This recognition drives us to keep raising the standard of the education we offer, said Sunway University president and vice-chancellor Prof Sibrandes Poppema. The AppliedEdu approach gives greatest weight to teaching and learning, which accounts for 40% of the assessment. Employability contributes a further 20% for private universities and 15% for public universities. Together, these measures represent 60% and 55% of the respective scores, making the quality of education and graduate student outcomes central to the results. The Asean rankings weigh six criteria: Teaching & Learning (40%), Employability (15% public, 20% private), Research (15% public, 10% private), Institutional Reputation, Community Engagement and Internationalisation (10% each). Public and private universities are never ranked together: each has its own methodology and weights, reflecting the different missions they serve. Rankings should do more than recognise achievement; they should drive improvement, said AppliedEdu chief executive officer and founder Mandy Mok. They should help universities build on their strengths, identify where change is needed, and make informed decisions that deliver better outcomes for students and the communities they serve.

KUALA LUMPUR: The Dewan Rakyat took a linguistic twist on Wednesday (Oct 21) when Sabak Bernam MP Kalam Salan switched to Javanese to deliver a message to Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto over the annual haze. Kalam said he would speak in Javanese, suggesting that leaders on the Indonesian side might not understand Malay. To the respected Pak Prabowo, please take immediate action to put out the fires, stop the burning and ensure this problem does not recur every year. We want clear skies, clean air and for the people of both countries to live healthily and peacefully, he said during the Budget 2027 debate. Kalam also took issue with remarks by an Indonesian leader suggesting that the republics forests had long supplied oxygen to Malaysia. Let us not turn this issue into a joke by claiming that Indonesias forests provide oxygen to Malaysia. Are Malaysias trees made of plastic? Can they not produce oxygen? he asked. He also called on the government to use diplomatic channels to urge the Philippines, which holds the Asean chairmanship this year, to take stronger regional action against transboundary haze. He proposed five measures, including stronger joint enforcement, a regional early warning system using satellite monitoring and real-time hotspot data, and a regional emergency response team to tackle fires before the haze spreads across borders. Beyond the policy proposals, Kalam also highlighted health aspects affecting Malaysians, who were left struggling with breathing difficulties, itchy throats, coughing and worsening asthma. Schools had to close, tourism was affected and plantation work could not proceed, he said. He added that Indonesians working on Malaysian plantations were also affected, as disruptions to their work could leave them without wages and unable to send money home to their families.

PETALING JAYA: Umno Youth chief Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh will be selling his motorcycle and farmed tilapia fish to raise the RM300,000 in damages awarded to Seputeh MP Teresa Kok in her defamation suit against him. Dr Akmal said he respects the court order and is ready to comply. "RM300,000 is a big amount for me and even after taking into account my savings, it is still not enough," he said on Facebook on Wednesday (Oct 21). "With a heavy heart, I am offering to sell off my two beloved assets  my motorcycle and bred tilapias. "Both hold their own stories of struggle and happiness for me. "Even writing that I intend to sell them feels difficult as it is hard to part with something we love." He also urged interested buyers to message him privately with their offers. "If both parties can agree on a price, we will proceed," he said. Dr Akmal also expressed gratitude for those who expressed concern and encouragement. "However, please allow me to try to raise the money on my own first. "I know that each of you also have families, financial commitments and difficulties of your own," he said. Dr Akmal said it would weigh even more heavily on him to burden others when he still has possessions to liquidate. On Monday (Oct 19), Kok won her defamation suit against Dr Akmal at the Melaka High Court. Justice Datuk Isa Aziz Ibrahim ordered him to pay RM250,000 in damages and RM50,000 in costs over remarks concerning halal certification. The court also ordered him to remove the offending posts within seven days and barred him from repeating the defamatory statements, according to Koks lawyer Datuk Sankara Nair. Kok filed the suit in October 2024 over statements Dr Akmal made in a TikTok video posted on Sept 7 that year. In her statement of claim, she alleged that the remarks insulted and belittled her, portraying her as lacking knowledge of halal certification and opposing government policies on Islamic practices. She named Dr Akmal, the incumbent Merlimau assemblyman, as the sole defendant and sought damages and an injunction to prevent him from repeating the statements.

KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia continues to view with great concern the dangerous escalation of conflict unfolding across the Middle East, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. Anwar said he has been in close contact with key regional leaders, including Saudi Arabia's Crown Prince Mohammed Salman and Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed Abdulrahman Al Thani. According to him, these high-level discussions reflect the utmost gravity with which Malaysia regards the crisis and the urgent need to prevent it from widening further. "Malaysias position is clear as we remain steadfast in our call for peace and justice for the Palestinian people, our unequivocal condemnation of the genocide in Gaza and our opposition to the indiscriminate bombing of southern Lebanon," he said in a post on X on Wednesday (Oct 21). He emphasised that this same moral conviction compels Malaysia to speak out with equal firmness whenever innocent civilians are targeted anywhere else. Consequently, Malaysia reiterates its strong condemnation of attacks by the Houthi movement against civilians and critical civilian infrastructure, such as airports and energy installations in Saudi Arabia and other Gulf Cooperation Council states. He also noted that the recent strike on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, which claimed the lives of innocent civilians, including pilgrims, served as a reminder of the human toll of such violence. The Prime Minister clarified that Malaysia's firm stance targets those responsible for the aggression rather than the resilient people of Yemen, who have suffered years of hardship and deserve a lasting political settlement. Furthermore, he stressed that maintaining the security of the Middle East's vital sea lanes is paramount for a trading nation like Malaysia. "Malaysia will continue to support all diplomatic efforts to de-escalate the crisis and safeguard the freedom of navigation," Anwar said.  Bernama

CYBERJAYA: The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) has recorded the statement of an individual to assist in an investigation of Facebook content suspected to contain elements insulting the Negri Sembilan royal institution. In a statement on Wednesday (Oct 21), MCMC said the action was taken to complete an investigation under Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998. "The individual believed to be operating the account appeared at the Cyberjaya police station today to assist in the investigation, and one mobile phone and one SIM card were seized," MCMC said. It is investigating content uploaded through the Facebook account "Che GuBard", which is suspected of containing elements insulting the Negri Sembilan royal institution, as well as touching on Yang di-Pertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir and members of the Negri Sembilan royal family. MCMC said it took a serious view of any use of online platforms that could incite hatred, insults or disrespect towards the royal institution. "Freedom of expression must be exercised responsibly and in accordance with the laws of the country. Any further action will be taken based on the findings of the investigation and the applicable legal process," MCMC said.  Bernama

KUALA LUMPUR: Pasir Gudang MP Hassan Abdul Karim has expressed disappointment over the absence of ministers during his Budget 2027 debate, saying he wanted to support the governments proposals but no ministers were there to hear his views. "I am a government backbencher and I want to support this Budget. There are many good things in it, but my friends in the Opposition are here to listen to me. The government is not here," he said in the Dewan Rakyat on Wednesday (Oct 21). Hassan also urged the government to ensure fairer allocations for all 222 MPs, saying funding should not depend solely on the Prime Ministers discretion. He called for a Bill to establish a system that binds both the current administration and future governments to distribute constituency allocations fairly. "If one constituency receives RM3mil or RM4mil, others should receive the same amount," he said. On Sabah and Sarawak, Hassan welcomed the higher federal allocations for both states under Budget 2027, but called for a fairer distribution of the countrys wealth and natural resources. He said the Petroleum Development Act 1974 should be reviewed to ensure a fairer arrangement for Sabah and Sarawak, as well as Terengganu and Kelantan. He also stressed that Putrajaya must respect the Federal Constitution, the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) and relevant court decisions concerning Sabah and Sarawak. "We love Sabah and Sarawak, just as our friends there love Peninsular Malaysia," he said, adding that helping the two states prosper would benefit the country as a whole. Hassan also said Malaysians should not fear a change of government as long as Parliament could perform its checks and balances role and key institutions remained independent and professional. "Building a nation takes time, but destroying it can happen very quickly," he said.

KUCHING: Police have detained a 16-year-old student who reportedly injured a teacher with an axe at a private school here on Wednesday (Oct 21). Sarawak acting police commissioner Deputy Comm Saifullizan Ishak said police received an emergency call at 8.03am informing them that the student had brought firecrackers to the school and injured a female teacher. The teacher was reported to have sustained cuts on her hand. "We are conducting detailed investigations to identify the cause of the incident and obtain evidence," he said in a statement. The case is being investigated under Section 324 of the Penal Code for voluntarily causing hurt with a dangerous weapon and Section 6(1) of the Explosives Act 1957. Meanwhile, the student allegedly livestreamed the incident through a mobile phone attached to his forehead. The video, which has been widely circulated, shows the student getting ready in the restroom before heading out into the corridor. A CCTV recording of a classroom, which has also gone viral, shows the student entering and approaching the teacher with an axe, before she restrains him with the help of another student.

PETALING JAYA: Schools in Selangor and Kuala Lumpur will remain open on Thursday (Oct 22). The Selangor Education Department said on Wednesday (Oct 21) that outdoor activities are suspended, and students attending school are encouraged to wear face masks. Administrators must continuously monitor the Air Pollutant Index (API) readings from the Environment Department (DOE) and pay special attention to high-risk students. "Parents or guardians who are concerned about their children's health may choose not to send them to school, provided they notify the school," the department said in a statement.
